title: Enterprise on‑prem orchestration: quarterly plan, stakeholder scenarios, and initiative mapping
creator: Priya Desai
description:
Summary:
This ticket consolidates the quarterly roadmap for enterprise Private/VPC/On‑Prem deployments into an actionable plan with scenario-based stakeholder outcomes. Goal is to produce a prioritized initiative map, identify cross-team dependencies, and surface risk mitigations so Sales/PS/SRE can commit to GTM timelines.

Objectives:
- Deliver a sequenced roadmap for Q2–Q3 that balances SLA guarantees, upgrade safety, and manageable engineering scope.
- Produce stakeholder scenarios (Minimal Viable Onprem, Secure Compliance Wave, High‑Availability Wave) that map features to customer segments and OKR targets.
- Identify top 6 cross-team dependencies and assign owners to de-risk delivery.
- Create a measurable success rubric (uptime SLO adherence, time-to-deploy for new customers, install rollback rate).

Scope (in/out):
In scope: private control plane improvements, on‑prem installer UX, VPC routing templates, KMS integrations, upgrade playbook automation, basic RBAC/audit hooks.
Out of scope this quarter: bespoke managed hosting for single large accounts, full air‑gapped certified appliance, advanced multi‑cluster federation.

Success metrics / OKRs alignment:
- OKR: Reduce median private deploy onboarding time from 14 days -> 7 days (metric: time from contract to first successful inference request).
- OKR: Achieve 99.9% uptime for Dedicated and Private customers post‑GA (SLO target).
- OKR: <2% install rollback rate across all installs in pilot cohort.

Milestones and timeline (high level):
- Week 1–2: Finalize initiative mapping & scenario definitions; stakeholder review (PM, Eng Tech Leads, SRE, Sales Eng).
- Week 3–6: Draft rollout waves, dependency assignments, and resource commitments.
- Week 7–10: Implementation planning: epics created in ENG backlog, infra reservations requested, security review kickoff.
- Week 11–12: Pilot release planning and acceptance criteria defined; customer pilot outreach.

Key deliverables:
- Initiative map PDF and CSV (link below).
- Dependency matrix with named owners and mitigation options.
- Release gating checklist and upgrade rollback playbook stub.
- Communication plan for enterprise customers and internal GTM.

Stakeholders:
- PM leads: Priya Desai (owner), Connor Blake (GTM), Lena Fischer (security liaison).
- Eng leads: Omar Okoye (runtime), Miguel Torres (private deploy), Asha Patel (SRE).
- Sales/PS: Katerina Ivanov (AE), Raj Malhotra (PS).

Major risks & proposed mitigations:
- Risk: Kernel/runtime incompatibilities during quantized model upgrades causing degraded latency. Mitigation: Hold compatibility gate; require perf test pass on representative workloads (ENG-30421).
- Risk: Security accreditation (FIPS/KMS) delays blocking pilot customers. Mitigation: Parallelize security review and automate key parts of audit evidence collection.
- Risk: Resource contention for GPU capacity affecting Dedicated customers during pilot. Mitigation: Reserve burst capacity and specify fallback routes to hosted variants.

Open decisions required from leadership:
1) Prioritization tradeoff: ship upgrade automation (higher churn, large payoff) vs. ship richer RBAC & audit features (lower churn, necessary for regulated customers). Decision needed by 2026-03-18.
2) Pilot cohort size: 5 customers (faster iteration) vs 12 customers (more representative). Decision needed by 2026-03-22.

Artifacts and references:
- Initiative map (draft): https://confluence.redwood.ai/private-deploy-initiative/initiative-map-draft-2026Q2
- Dependency matrix (sheet): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-init-matrix
- Upgrade playbook (working doc): https://confluence.redwood.ai/private-deploy-initiative/upgrade-playbook-stub
- Runtime compatibility checklist PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/742
- Pilot outreach template (Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/pilot-outreach-templates

Next steps (owner):
- Miguel: convert initiative map rows into ENG epics and link dependencies (due 2026-03-19).
- Priya: run stakeholder alignment readout and collect leadership decision on tradeoff (due 2026-03-18).
- Connor: draft GTM pilot email & PSA for existing enterprise customers (due 2026-03-24).

Notes on trade‑offs considered during scoping:
- Time vs. breadth: Narrower initial feature set reduces integration risk but may limit which customers can pilot. We intentionally prioritize core install/upgrade safety first to reduce customer churn risk.
- Security vs. speed: Some compliance controls add 3–6 weeks; we will gate on customer segment to allow faster pilots with lower compliance needs.

This ticket will be used to post meeting notes from the roadmap workshop and to record final leadership decisions. Attachments and updated artifacts will be linked here as they are finalized.
